newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet sells aircraft, retires debt.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet sells aircraft, retires debt.

text.p: ValuJet Inc said Tuesday it had sold three surplus aircraft and the pre-paid financing debt on a fourth aircraft.
The transactions enabled ValuJet to retire $18.7 million of aircraft bank debt. ValuJet said it sold the aircraft at or above the company's book value.

"ValuJet continues to move aggressively toward further reducing surplus aircraft capacity and associated debt," said ValuJet Chief Financial Officer Steve Nevin. "We are sizing our fleet to allow moderate growth without unnecessary ownership expense."
ValuJet sold its remaining MD-83 aircraft, including its MD-80 spare parts inventory. This transaction concludes the removal of the MD-80 aircraft type and supporting spares from ValuJet.
ValuJet also sold two surplus DC-9-32 aircraft, bringing ValuJet's fleet to 43 DC-9 series 30 aircraft.
The airline also pre-paid the debt on another DC-9-32 aircraft that ValuJet plans to sell during the first quarter 1997.
